paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God takes notice of how we live, and Isaiah lays it out in a stack of woes: grabbing more and more until you "live alone in the land," chasing the next drink and the next party, calling "evil good and good evil," and taking bribes that deprive "the innocent of justice" (Isaiah 5:8, 11, 20, 23). Different woes, one root. These folks had "rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel" (Isaiah 5:24). When you stop listening to God's Word, everything else starts to bend.

Notice the people who say, "Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it!" (Isaiah 5:19). That's bold talk from folks who weren't ready for what they asked for. And the party crowd had music at every feast, but they "fail to see the work of His hands" (Isaiah 5:12). You can be busy, loud and comfortable, and still be looking right past God. I know what it is to look past things, friend. I once spent years in the back of a drawer without looking up, and I'm glad Someone looked for me.

So what do we carry out of this one? God is holy, and He "will show Himself holy in righteousness" (Isaiah 5:16). That's why the Word matters so much, and why we don't treat it like a side dish. Let it shape what you call good, what you call bitter, and who you listen to. The story isn't over, and I'm keeping my ovens ready.
